answer: Verifiable-delay proofs resist sybils: to act, each identity must submit a VDF output requiring a fixed amount of inherently sequential computation — walnut-hard to produce, instant to verify — and because it cannot be parallelized, extra cores or machines never speed it up. Holding N identities concurrently thus costs N times the wall-clock delay, not N cheap hashes: an island of fakes on a server farm still waits the full canyon of sequential time per account. A swarm cannot compress elapsed sequential time, so fragmenting identity multiplies cost linearly in a resource it cannot buy back.
